market_holds: Spot about $59.7-60.2 (sealed 18:09 UTC; Yahoo bars). That is an all-time high, -1.4% from the 52-week high, and roughly double the $29.85 pre-Q2 close of 2026-08-12. Run-up is +14.9% over 5 days and +17.3% over 20. The front-week straddle implies about 21.4%, about 19.7% event-only. ATM IV is 171%, the 25-delta put skew is +32 vol points, and put/call open interest is 3.9, so downside protection is being paid for. Short interest per Nasdaq was 5.69M shares on 2026-10-30, down from 7.33M on 10-15, about 6-7% of roughly 86M shares, 3.5 days to cover. Consensus per Yahoo Analysis (9 analysts): Q3 revenue $65.2M (range $64.6-65.9M), Q4 $66.7M, FY26 $248.6M, which is the midpoint of the $246-250M guide set 2026-08-13. FY27 is $308.6M (+24%). The EPS trend for the quarter has been flat at -$0.10 for 60 days, so the numbers are anchored to the guide and about 90 days old. The price is far above the sell-side: average target about $50 per stockanalysis (high $64, Piper 2026-10-20). Market cap is about $5.2B, about 17x FY27 consensus revenue. The last reactions: +35.7% on Q2 (big beat, $18M raise, from a depressed base), -12.2% on Q1 (beat of about 5%, $10M raise), +1.7% on Q4'25 and -13.4% on Q3'25. So the stock trades on the size of the beat and raise against an elevated expectation, not on the beat itself.
view: A beat and raise is the base case, and the market knows it. On the Q2 call the CFO said the guide assumes 'steady sequential growth in both Q3 and Q4', is a 'high conviction baseline' and leaves 'room to outperform'. Consensus $65.2M is only +1.7% on Q2's $64.1M, while FFRct volumes in Q2 came in 'significantly above plan'. My own arithmetic: Q2 FFRct was about $56.3M ($64.1M less $7.8M plaque). Hold FFRct flat to +3% for the seasonality management flagged, and let plaque step to about $9-10M (needed for the $29-31M FY plaque guide). That gives Q3 of about $66.5-69M, a beat of 2-6%. RadNet's Q3 (CT volume +22%, same-center advanced imaging +8.9% against 9.6% in Q2) supports steady demand, not a step-up. The OPPS/PFS CY2027 final rule (2026-11-04) kept SaMS rates near CY2026, which is neutral. The Nov 1-2 P4/NEJM and DECIDE/AHA data are supportive but public. Against that, the stock has doubled since the last print, sits at an all-time high above every target but one, and ran +16% in the five sessions into the print against SPY +3.5% and IHI -2%. Half of that was a rebound from the 11-05 market selloff to the late-October high. The likely beat is smaller than Q2's (about 13% against guide-implied consensus). On this name a beat of about 5% with a mid-size raise has led to -12% (Q1) and +2% (Q4'25). The buy-side whisper is therefore plausibly near $68-70M plus a raise to the mid-$250Ms. My central estimate of the print sits about there, so I cannot say which side of the real bar the release lands on. The put-heavy book and moderate, declining short interest set the size of the move more than its direction.

recommendation.reason: The published consensus is stale and sits below the likely print, but the price ($60, far above the ~$50 average target, doubled since August, +16% in five days) shows the buy-side already expects a beat and raise. My estimate of the print ($66.5-69M plus a raise) is about where a plausible whisper sits. No dated evidence puts the deciding line (FY raise size, and any early 2027 framing against a +24% FY27 consensus) clearly above or below what the price holds.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q3 above about $70M with FY guide lifted to $258M or more, or explicit 2027 growth framing well above the +24% consensus, would make this an up print. Q3 near $65-66M with a token raise would make it a down print, as on Q1.

self_critique: The upside case: the company has beaten and raised three quarters running, said outright that it left room, and its plaque line is ramping on the Category I code and broad commercial coverage. The FY27 consensus of +24% is visibly too low for a 45% grower. A Q3 of $70M+ and a raise to $260M could squeeze a put-heavy, still 6%-shorted name 20%+. The downside case: the stock doubled and sits above almost every target, the beat should be smaller than Q2's, and Q1 shows this name sells a modest beat. Both cases are plausible and I have no dated evidence that separates them, so I stay at 50 rather than lean.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped: it separated the 11-05 market drop and the rebound from company news. P4's stale-consensus check pointed to a likely beat, but the price itself showed that beat is expected, so P7's 'estimate the line' still left me at 50. I could find no whisper or preview, which is the piece that would decide this name.
